newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah threatens anti-Israeli suicide bombings.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah threatens anti-Israeli suicide bombings.

text.p: The militant pro-Iranian Moslem group Hizbollah threatened on Friday to launch suicide bombers against Israeli forces if they mounted a new offensive in Lebanon.

"I promise and threaten this enemy that any new aggression against Lebanon will drag the occupying Israeli army back into mud and into a quagmire where bombs are not made of iron but of human bodies," Hizbollah chief Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah said.

"All of us are ready...to present our blood for the sake of our people and its dignity and freedom," the cleric told an election rally in eastern Lebanon's Bekaa Valley broadcast live by Hizbollah's al-Manar television in Beirut.

Nasrallah was speaking hours after Israeli helicopters fired rockets into suspected Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrilla targets in south Lebanon, heightening fears that Israel may mount a large scale offensive.

A senior Lebanese official said on Thursday Beirut was taking seriously a warning by Israel's client South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia of possible wide Israeli retaliation if Hizbollah stepped up attacks on Israeli troops.
But SLA chief General Antoine Lahd said on Friday he was expressing his own analysis rather than conveying a message from Israel.

Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Friday he would raise the issue -- discussed by Lebanese and Syrian officials on Thursday -- at a weekend Arab foreign ministers meeting in Cairo to discuss the Middle East peace process.
The bearded Nasrallah said Hizbollah guerrillas, who had weathered large-scale Israeli offensives in July 1993 and April 1996, were ready for any new confrontation.
"I tell the Israeli enemy that we will fight in every village and in every sector," the black-turbaned cleric said.
"We will remain the resistance that liberates (the land) and the resistance that defends," he added.
The crowd of tens of thousands of militants, including women in Iranian-style Islamic dress, chanted back the fundamentalist group's rallying cry: "War, War until victory".

Hizbollah leads an Islamic Resistance vying to oust Israel's 1,000 troops and the 3,000-strong SLA from a south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to prevent raids on northern Israel. They have killed 18 Israeli soldiers in Lebanon since January.

Friday's air attack against a Hizbollah mountain stronghold used to attack the Israeli-held zone came hours after Israeli soldiers ambushed fighters of the group who had infiltrated the border strip, killing one guerrilla.
Hizbollah claimed responsiblity for the infiltration and said its guerrillas wounded several Israeli soldiers in an ambush against their patrol.

Israel launched a bloody 17-day onslaught -- dubbed "Operation Grapes of Wrath" -- against Hizbollah in April, killing 200 people, mostly civilians, after bombardments of civilian areas by the two sides.

An April 26 understanding that ended the fighting banned both parties from firing from or at civilian targets on both sides of the Israel-Lebanon border. However, it did not rule out guerrilla attacks on Israeli troops inside Lebanon.
